reference_memory.normal_pattern: The time series exhibits a highly regular, quasi-sinusoidal oscillation with an estimated period of ~183 points, consistent across all candidates. Each cycle features a sharp, asymmetric rise (steep positive slope) followed by a slower, smoother decay (gentle negative slope), forming a characteristic sawtooth-like waveform with rounded peaks and sharper troughs. Baseline level is stable near zero (robust median ≈ 0.1–0.3), with no significant long-term drift in the multi-cycle segments; candidate 0 shows a negligible upward slope per point (2.5e-4) but remains flat within noise. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is tightly clustered around 4.6–4.8 robust standardized units, with peak values consistently between 3.4–4.2 and troughs near –1.0 to –0.8. Noise is low: roughness (~0.032) and curvature (~0.015) are nearly identical across candidates, indicating smooth, deterministic morphology with minimal high-frequency jitter. Boundary truncation is present in candidate 0 (single cycle, cut at both ends), but its internal shape matches the rising/decaying motif of full cycles. All multi-cycle candidates (1–3) show near-perfect phase alignment and morphological consistency across repetitions—peaks are symmetrically rounded, troughs are shallow and broad, and inter-peak intervals are uniform. Acceptable variation includes minor shifts in absolute baseline (±0.1), slight differences in peak sharpness (candidate 3 slightly sharper), and negligible trend offsets (<0.001 per point), all within robust statistical tolerance.
